New to Ọkpan? We recommend starting by adding at least one institution, then importing your first dataset.

Okpan accepts CSV, JSON, and XML files. CSV is the most common format — most museum databases and spreadsheet tools can export to it. JSON and XML are more structured formats often used by developer APIs or custom database exports.
Check our tutorials to know how to get data from institutions.
Connect the columns in your file to the fields in Okpan. Your file may call things differently — "Medium" instead of "Material", for example.

Okpan uses this to tell objects apart and to update existing records safely if you re-import the same file in the future.

Okpan tries to match each asset to an object by comparing the filename with the object identifier and any additional search fields you select.
If a match isn't correct, click the edit button to change it manually. Assets that don't match any object can be linked later from the object page.
